arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Schnapper argued the sides that brought the case propose substantial legal changes.
He claimed this involves fundamental changes in federal-state relations.
Mr. Sutton stated it is never appropriate to imply private rights.
He argued this under the federal spending power context.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether Title VI regulations allow private individuals to sue for damages. The dispute centers on the scope of federal spending power.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome defines the scope of federal anti-discrimination enforcement. It determines whether individuals can sue directly for Title VI violations. This shapes the balance between federal and state authority.
